mainTopic: Finishing the dispute about volunteer guards; damage from manure and building materials in רשות הרבים; who pays among builders; and vegetables growing between two gardens
overview: The גמרא first explains what the חכמים meant when they answered רבי יוסי with 'אתה אומר?'. It then gives רבין's report, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that their dispute depends on whether we worry about בעלי זרועות. A new משנה teaches that manure, clay and building stones may not be left lying in רשות הרבים, and that whoever causes damage must pay. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a person to prepare his building materials thirty days ahead. The גמרא shows that this משנה does not follow רבי יהודה, who exempts anyone the חכמים allowed to use the street. אביי adds that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי שמעון hold the same view. A ברייתא then explains which worker pays when a building stone causes damage, and the גמרא settles a contradiction by separating hired workers (שכירות) from a contract job (קבלנות). Finally, a new משנה discusses who owns vegetables growing between an upper and a lower garden. רבא explains that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about the leaves, and a ברייתא about a tree's sprouts shows each keeps his own reasoning.

steps.title: What did the Sages mean by 'You say?'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant when they answered רבי יוסי with the short phrase 'אתה אומר?'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'You say?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier teaching it was discussing, the משנה in שקלים about guarding the ספיחין, and asks about one puzzling phrase. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, רבי יוסי said a person may volunteer to do the guarding for free. The חכמים answered only 'אתה אומר?' ('You say so?'). The גמרא wants to know what exactly they were objecting to.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You say?', a short reply that shows surprise or disagreement

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "you say"?
phrases.notes: This quotes the חכמים's short reply to רבי יוסי in the משנה the גמרא was just discussing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה ״אַתָּה אוֹמֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the משנה from before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What objection the חכמים were raising with the words 'אתה אומר?'

steps.title: Your view would mean the public offerings are not paid by the public
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים were telling רבי יוסי that if we combine his view with theirs, the daily and additional offerings would no longer come entirely from public funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were saying to him: If we combine your words with our words, the תמידין and מוספין would not come from public funds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The חכמים were pointing out a problem that follows from רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that the worker is paid from public money. If someone works for free, as רבי יוסי allows, then part of what goes into the public offerings comes as a private gift. That breaks the rule that קרבנות צבור must come from the public.

keyTerms.meaning: From your words to our words: combining your view with ours
The daily offerings and the additional offerings of שבת and יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that קרבנות צבור must be fully owned by the community, not partly given by one person.

phrases.english: This is what they were saying to him:
From your words to our words,
phrases.notes: In plain English: 'If we put your rule together with ours.'

phrases.english: the daily and additional offerings do not come from public funds.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, to make clear which offerings are meant.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים meant that רבי יוסי's view leads to public offerings that are not fully paid for by the public

steps.title: רבין: the dispute is about worrying over powerful people
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן said the real difference between רבי יוסי and the חכמים is whether we worry about בעלי זרועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The difference between them is whether we are concerned about strong-armed people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second explanation of the same dispute. רבין names the central issue that divides the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the main issue is a practical worry, not only the rule about public money. If we worry that powerful people might take what is not theirs, a paid guard is needed. רבי יוסי does not share this worry, so he is fine with a volunteer.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Strong-armed people, those who use force
This is the difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין, the dispute between רבי יוסי and the חכמים depends on whether we worry about בעלי זרועות.

phrases.english: And likewise, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
whether we are concerned about strong-armed people
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation of the same dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי יוסי and the חכמים depends on whether we are concerned about בעלי זרועות

steps.title: משנה: manure and clay in the public road
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says manure taken into רשות הרבים must be moved on right away. Clay may not be soaked and bricks may not be formed there, but clay may be kneaded there.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who takes manure out to the public domain: the one taking it out takes it out, and the one fertilizing takes it right away to fertilize. One may not soak clay in the public domain or form bricks there. But one may knead clay in the public domain, though not bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets limits on using the public road for slow jobs that would get in people's way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Short jobs are allowed in the public road, but long jobs that block it are not. Manure must keep moving, and soaking clay or forming bricks takes too long. Kneading clay is quick, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, a street or road everyone uses

steps.confusionAlert: 'המוציא מוציא והמזבל מזבל' does not mean anyone may do as he likes. It means the work must flow without a break: as soon as the manure comes out, it is carried off to the field.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who takes manure out to the public domain,
the one who takes it out takes it out,
and the one who fertilizes takes it to fertilize.
phrases.notes: He means it right away: the manure cannot just sit in the street.

phrases.english: One may not soak clay in the public domain,
and one may not form bricks.
But one may knead clay in the public domain,
but not bricks.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹצִיא זֶבֶל לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Manure must be moved on at once, and slow work like soaking clay or forming bricks is not allowed in רשות הרבים. Quick kneading is allowed.

steps.title: משנה: building stones in the public road, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Building stones brought into רשות הרבים must be used right away, and the owner pays for any damage. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets a person prepare his materials thirty days ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who builds using the public domain: the one bringing stones brings them, and the builder builds right away. If they cause damage, he pays for what was damaged. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He may even prepare his work thirty days ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with building materials. It ends with a disagreement from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses the same 'keep it moving' rule as with manure, and adds that the owner pays for damage. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives more room: materials may sit in the street for up to thirty days before building.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepares his work (gets his materials ready)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה wants רשות הרבים kept clear. Only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a thirty-day preparation period. According to the first opinion, anyone who causes damage must pay.

phrases.english: One who builds, using the public domain,
the one who brings stones brings them,
and the one who builds builds with them right away.
And if it caused damage, he pays for what it damaged.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
He may even prepare his work
thirty days beforehand.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבּוֹנֶה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with building materials
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building stones must be used right away and any damage must be paid for. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows thirty days of preparation.

steps.title: Does the משנה disagree with רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה, which does not let manure sit in the street, goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that our משנה is not in line with רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a suggestion. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says manure must be moved at once. If some תנא allows manure to stay in the street for a long time, then the משנה cannot match his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
Shall we say (a suggestion that is often later rejected)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shall we say that our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's rule about manure goes against רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets manure be piled in the street for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: during manure season, a person may pile his manure in the street for thirty days so it gets trampled. This was a condition יהושע set when he divided the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, at the time when manure is taken out, a person may take his manure into the public domain and pile it there for thirty days, so it gets trampled by the feet of people and animals. It was on this condition that יהושע gave the land to ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that makes the suggestion of step 6 look right. רבי יהודה clearly allows manure to sit in the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires manure to be moved at once, but רבי יהודה allows thirty days of piling, so the two seem to clash. His reason is that trampling prepares the manure, and that the land was given to ישראל on the understanding that people put up with this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ownership of the land came with built-in conditions that help everyone. Some public use is allowed because יהושע set it up that way.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
At the time of taking out manure,
a person may take his manure out to the public domain
and pile it up for all thirty days,
so that it will be trampled
by the feet of people and the feet of animals,
since it was on this condition
that Joshua gave the land to the Jewish people as an inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the suggestion in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not match רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה allows manure to be piled in רשות הרבים for thirty days

steps.title: רבי יהודה may agree that damage must be paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can still follow רבי יהודה, because even he agrees that a person pays if his manure causes damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה agrees that if it causes damage, the owner must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6 by saying our משנה can still match רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows manure in the street for thirty days. The answer suggests he only gives permission to put it there, and the owner still pays for any damage. On this reading, the משנה's rule about damage fits him too.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Used to show a source fits an opinion it seemed to go against.
Agrees. One side admits a point to the other.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
because Rabbi Yehuda agrees
that if it caused damage, he must pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 6, which was supported by the ברייתא in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits permission to act from liability for damage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה allows manure in the street, the משנה, which makes the owner pay for damage, seemed to go against him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה only allows the manure to be there. He still makes the owner pay for damage, so the משנה can follow him.

steps.title: Challenge from the נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a משנה where רבי יהודה exempts someone whose נר חנוכה caused damage, because he acted with permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: רבי יהודה agrees that with a נר חנוכה the person is exempt, because he acts with permission. Doesn't that mean permission of the בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in Step 8. It shows that רבי יהודה exempts someone who acts with permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "permission" means the court let him use the street, then for רבי יהודה any court permission removes liability. That would include the manure, and the answer in Step 8 would fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The lamp lit for the מצוה of חנוכה
Doesn't it mean...? This suggests a reading of the source.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
Rabbi Yehuda agrees about a Chanukah lamp
that he is exempt,
because he acts with permission.
Doesn't this mean permission of the court?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנֵר חֲנוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה makes a person pay even when he acted with permission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה exempts the Chanukah lamp because of permission. If that means court permission, the same reason would exempt the manure.

steps.title: It means permission of a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נר חנוכה is exempt because it is a מצוה, not just because the בית דין allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means the permission of a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 8 by reading the "permission" in the case of the נר חנוכה as permission that comes from a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נר חנוכה is a מצוה, which is a stronger reason to exempt. Plain court permission, like for manure, might not exempt. So the נר חנוכה case does not prove that רבי יהודה exempts the manure owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission that comes from doing a מצוה

phrases.english: No, it means the permission of a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רְשׁוּת דְּמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Permission" means court permission, so any court-allowed use is exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Permission" means a מצוה, so only the נר חנוכה gets this special exemption.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה exempts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that in all the cases where people may put obstacles in the street they pay for damage, but רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: in all the cases where the חכמים said a person may make obstacles in the street, if they cause damage he must pay, and רבי יהודה exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. A ברייתא clearly says רבי יהודה exempts people who were allowed to make obstacles in the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This has nothing to do with a מצוה. It is plain permission to use the street, the same as manure. So the answer from Step 10 does not help, and Step 8 cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a mess or put obstacles

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
All these cases where they said
that people may put obstacles in the public street,
if it caused damage, he must pay,
and Rabbi Yehuda exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כׇּל אֵלּוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מוּתָּרִין לְקַלְקֵל בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 10 answered the challenge from the נר חנוכה, this is a new and stronger challenge to Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 8 that רבי יהודה makes the owner pay for damage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly says רבי יהודה exempts anyone allowed to put obstacles in the street. That is plain permission, not a מצוה.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its answer and concludes that our משנה goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on fitting the משנה with רבי יהודה and accepts what Step 6 first suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא proves that רבי יהודה exempts damage done with permission, he cannot agree with a משנה that makes the owner pay. So the משנה follows a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is clear. This drops the earlier answer.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, someone the חכמים allowed to use the public street does not pay for damage that results. Our משנה, which makes him pay, does not follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that
our משנה does not follow Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in Step 11 and closes the question from Step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה goes against רבי יהודה, who exempts damage done with the חכמים' permission.

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים exempt anyone acting with permission
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי יהודה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי שמעון all hold that if the חכמים gave permission and damage happened, the person is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי יהודה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי שמעון all hold that wherever the חכמים gave a person permission and he caused damage, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the rule just learned about רבי יהודה and says two more תנאים share it. Next he will bring a source for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that permission from the חכמים takes away liability for damage. אביי shows this is not only רבי יהודה's view but a shared position of three תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general rule: permission from the חכמים can free a person from paying for damage. That idea reaches well beyond manure.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and Rabbi Shimon
all hold:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים רְשׁוּת
phrases.english: wherever the Sages gave a person permission
and he caused damage, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion about רבי יהודה and widens it to two more תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For these three תנאים, whoever acts with the חכמים' permission is exempt from damage that results.

steps.title: Sources for רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: אביי's source for רבי יהודה is the ברייתא just quoted. His source for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is our משנה, which lets a person prepare his materials thirty days ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה: from what we just said. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: as we learned, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a person may even prepare his work thirty days ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving אביי's claim, one תנא at a time, beginning with רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the משנה made the owner pay for damage. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagreed and allowed thirty days of preparation. אביי reads his disagreement as covering payment too, so with permission there is no payment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda: from what we just said.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: as we learned in the משנה:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
he may even prepare his work
thirty days ahead.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first two sources for אביי's claim in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל exempt damage done with permission
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in Step 11 for רבי יהודה, and our משנה (Step 5) for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: Source for רבי שמעון: the oven in the upper story
steps.stepSummary: A משנה requires a plaster floor under an oven or stove upstairs, and the חכמים still make the owner pay. רבי שמעון says the measurements exist so that, once they are kept, the owner is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון: as we learned, if someone sets up an oven in an upper story, there must be a plaster floor three handbreadths thick under it, and for a stove one handbreadth. If it causes damage, he pays for what it damaged. רבי שמעון says: these measurements were only given to teach that if it causes damage, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the third תנא, רבי שמעון. This finishes the proof of אביי's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says that even after keeping the safety measurements, the owner pays. רבי שמעון says the reason for the measurements is that someone who keeps them has acted with permission and is exempt. This matches אביי's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's three sources: רבי יהודה (obstacles in the street), רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (preparing building materials), and רבי שמעון (oven measurements). All three exempt someone who acted with the חכמים' permission.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon: as we learned in a משנה:
If he was setting it up in an upper story,
phrases.notes: "It" is an oven. The משנה is talking about where an oven may be placed.

phrases.english: there must be a plaster floor under it
three handbreadths thick,
and for a stove, one handbreadth.
And if it caused damage, he pays for what it damaged.
Rabbi Shimon says:
They gave all these measurements
only to teach that if it caused damage, he is exempt from paying.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דִּתְנַן: הָיָה מַעֲמִידוֹ בַּעֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and last source for אביי's claim in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון exempts damage done with permission
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about an oven in an upper story, where רבי שמעון says keeping the measurements makes the owner exempt

steps.title: The chain of workers and who is responsible at each stage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists each worker who handles a building stone. Whoever has just received the stone is responsible for damage. If the stone falls from the finished row of the wall, all of them pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: once the stonecutter hands the stone to the chiseler, the chiseler is responsible. Once the chiseler hands it to the donkey driver, the donkey driver is responsible. Once the donkey driver hands it to the porter, the porter is responsible. Once the porter hands it to the builder, the builder is responsible. Once the builder hands it to the master builder, the master builder is responsible. But if he set the stone on the row of the wall and it fell and caused damage, they all have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about damage caused by a building stone as it passes from worker to worker. Responsibility moves with the stone, but damage from the stone on the wall makes everyone pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At each stage, the worker who now holds the stone is the one in charge of it, so he alone pays. Once the stone is set on the wall row, it is the product of everyone's work together, so all of them share the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Stonecutter: the one who cuts the stone out of the quarry
Chiseler: the one who shapes and smooths the stone
Porter: carries the stone on his shoulder to the site
Master builder: places and straightens the stones in the wall
A row of stones in the wall

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A stonecutter who handed over the stone to the chiseler: the chiseler is liable.
A chiseler who handed it over to the donkey driver: the donkey driver is liable.
A donkey driver who handed it over to the porter: the porter is liable.
A porter who handed it over to the builder: the builder is liable.
A builder who handed it over to the master builder: the master builder is liable.
And if he placed a stone on the row of the wall
and it caused damage, they are all liable to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַחַצָּב שֶׁמָּסַר לַסַּתָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the street-obstacles discussion to a new ברייתא about damage caused by building stones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Responsibility passes to each worker as he receives the stone. Damage from a stone on the wall row makes all of them liable.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says only the last worker pays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא saying that only the last worker is liable and everyone else is exempt. This contradicts the 'all pay' ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the last one is liable and all the others are exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second ברייתא that says the opposite about the stone on the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said everyone pays when the stone falls from the wall. The second says only the last worker, the master builder, pays. Both cannot be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The last one in the chain

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: the last one is liable
and all of them are exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אַחֲרוֹן חַיָּיב וְכוּלָּן פְּטוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the final ruling of Step 16 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that all the workers pay when the stone on the wall row causes damage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two ברייתות: one says all pay, the other says only the last pays.

steps.title: Hired workers versus a contract job
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות are about different kinds of work deals. When workers are hired (שכירות), only the last pays. When they take on the job together as a contract (קבלנות), they all pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it is talking about hiring, and there it is talking about contracting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about two different kinds of work deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hired workers are each paid for their own task, so only the last one, who set the stone, is responsible for it. In a contract job the workers took on the whole job together, so they share responsibility for the finished wall.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult': the two sources are about different cases
Hired work: paid by the day or task
Contract work: taking on a whole job for a set price

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות stand. When workers are simply hired (שכירות), only the last pays. When they take on the job together as a contract (קבלנות), all of them pay.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it is about hiring,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the ברייתא where only the last worker pays.

phrases.english: there it is about contracting.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ברייתא where all of them pay, because they took the job on together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּשְׂכִירוּת, כָּאן בְּקַבְּלָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different work arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hired work means only the last worker pays. Contract work means all of them pay.

steps.title: New משנה: vegetables between an upper and a lower garden
steps.stepSummary: Two gardens sit one above the other, and vegetables grow out of the dirt wall between them. רבי מאיר says they belong to the upper owner. רבי יהודה says they belong to the lower owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two gardens, one above the other, with vegetables growing in between. רבי מאיר says they belong to the upper owner. רבי יהודה says they belong to the lower owner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a dispute over who owns vegetables growing from the dirt wall between two gardens on different levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper garden's soil forms the wall, while the lower garden is the open space the wall faces. Each owner has a claim, and the תנאים argue over whose claim wins.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי גַּנּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ,
phrases.english: Two gardens, one above the other,
and the vegetables are in between.
phrases.notes: They grow out of the side wall of dirt where the ground drops.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: they belong to the upper one.
Rabbi Yehuda says: they belong to the lower one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי גַּנּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ, וְהַיָּרָק בֵּינְתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה, unrelated to the builders' liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: רבי מאיר gives the vegetables to the upper owner, and רבי יהודה gives them to the lower owner.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: the upper owner can remove the dirt
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר argues that if the upper owner dug away his dirt, there would be no wall and no vegetables. So the vegetables are his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: if the upper owner wanted to take away his dirt, there would be no vegetables here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives the reason for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall of dirt belongs to the upper garden, and the upper owner could remove it at any time. Since the vegetables exist only because he leaves his dirt there, they belong to him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִרְצֶה הָעֶלְיוֹן לִיקַּח אֶת עֲפָרוֹ,
phrases.english: If the upper one wanted to take away his dirt,
there would be no vegetables here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם יִרְצֶה הָעֶלְיוֹן לִיקַּח אֶת עֲפָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי מאיר's ruling from Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that the vegetables belong to the upper owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the upper owner can remove the dirt the vegetables grow from.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's answer: the lower owner can fill in his garden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה turns the same argument around. If the lower owner filled his garden up to the top, the wall would disappear and there would be no vegetables, so they are his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: if the lower owner wanted to fill up his garden, there would be no vegetables here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers רבי מאיר with the same kind of argument, pointing the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lower owner can also make the vegetables disappear, by raising his ground to cover the wall. So רבי מאיר's argument proves nothing special for the upper owner.

keyTerms.meaning: To fill up, here meaning to raise the ground with dirt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִרְצֶה הַתַּחְתּוֹן לְמַלֹּאות אֶת גִּנָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: If the lower one wanted to fill up his garden,
there would be no vegetables here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם יִרְצֶה הַתַּחְתּוֹן לְמַלֹּאות אֶת גִּנָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's reasoning from Step 20 with a matching counter-argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's argument that the upper owner can make the vegetables disappear
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lower owner can make them disappear too, so the argument favors neither side.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: since both can block it, look where the vegetable draws its life
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר accepts that both owners can stop the growth, so that argument decides nothing. Instead, we check where the vegetable gets its nourishment from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: since each of them can stop the other, we look at where this vegetable lives from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר replies that the 'who can remove it' argument cancels out, and he offers a new test for deciding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side can block the other, so that argument no longer decides anything. The new test is natural: whichever garden's soil feeds the plant's roots is the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: To object or block: here, to prevent the growth
Lives, here meaning draws its nourishment

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאַחַר שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶן יְכוֹלִין לְמַחוֹת זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: Since the two of them can each block the other,
we see from where this vegetable lives.
phrases.notes: He means: which garden's soil is feeding it, above or below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מֵאַחַר שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶן יְכוֹלִין לְמַחוֹת זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the standoff created in Steps 20-21 by offering a new test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since both owners can block the growth, ownership is decided by where the vegetable draws its nourishment.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: whatever the upper owner can reach is his
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives a practical rule. Whatever vegetables the upper owner can reach by stretching out his hand belong to him, and the rest belong to the lower owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: anything the upper owner can stretch out his hand and take is his, and the rest belongs to the lower owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third opinion that splits the vegetables between the two owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving everything to one side, רבי שמעון divides the vegetables by a simple measure: how far the upper owner can reach down. What he can reach is his, and everything below that goes to the lower owner.
steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions on the vegetables between the gardens: רבי מאיר says upper, then 'look where it draws its life'. רבי יהודה says lower. רבי שמעון says the upper owner gets what he can reach, and the lower owner gets the rest.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהָעֶלְיוֹן יָכוֹל לִפְשׁוֹט אֶת יָדוֹ וְלִיטּוֹל –
phrases.english: Whatever the upper one can stretch out his hand and take,
it is his,
and the rest belongs to the lower one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: כׇּל שֶׁהָעֶלְיוֹן יָכוֹל לִפְשׁוֹט אֶת יָדוֹ וְלִיטּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third position in the משנה's dispute, different from both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upper owner gets whatever vegetables he can reach by hand, and the lower owner gets the rest.

steps.title: רבא explains that the argument is only about the leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees the root belongs to the upper owner. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about the leaves: do they follow the root or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא says: About the root of the vegetable, everyone agrees that it belongs to the upper owner. Where they argue is about its leaves. רבי מאיר holds: treat the leaves as following the root. רבי יהודה holds: we do not say the leaves follow the root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by narrowing down the argument in the משנה. רבא says the root clearly belongs to the upper owner, so the fight is only over the leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The root grows inside the upper owner's dirt, so nobody gives it to the lower owner. The leaves stick out over the lower garden's airspace. רבי מאיר says the leaves go with the root, so they belong to the upper owner. רבי יהודה says the leaves are judged separately, so they belong to the lower owner.

keyTerms.meaning: its root, the base of the plant
its leaves or branches, the part sticking out
everyone agrees (literally: the whole world does not argue)
cast the leaves after the root, meaning the leaves follow the root's owner
the upper one, the owner of the upper garden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה gives the whole plant to the lower owner. According to רבא, even רבי יהודה agrees the root belongs to the upper owner. He only gives the leaves to the lower owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle, whether the leaves follow the root, which the גמרא will now find in another case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava says:
Regarding its root, everyone agrees
that it belongs to the upper owner.
Where they disagree is about its leaves.
Rabbi Meir holds:
Cast its leaves after its root.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן שְׁדִי נוֹפוֹ בָּתַר עִיקָּרוֹ.
phrases.english: We do not say: Cast its leaves after its root.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּעִיקָּרוֹ, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First גמרא statement on the משנה. It redefines the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה (steps 19-22) as being only about the leaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The root belongs to the upper owner according to everyone. רבי מאיר says the leaves follow the root, and רבי יהודה says they do not.

steps.title: Both תנאים keep their same reasoning in the case of a tree's sprouts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה stay consistent. In a ברייתא about sprouts from a tree, רבי מאיר again makes everything follow the root and ground, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught in a ברייתא: Sprouts that come out of the trunk or out of the roots belong to the owner of the land. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: sprouts from the trunk belong to the owner of the tree, and sprouts from the roots belong to the owner of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the argument רבא described matches what each תנא says in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives even the trunk sprouts to the land owner, because everything follows the root in the ground. That is the same idea as "cast the leaves after the root." רבי יהודה gives the trunk sprouts to the tree owner, which shows he does not make everything follow the root.

keyTerms.meaning: they follow their own reasoning, staying consistent with their views

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: what sticks out follows the root, so the leaves and trunk sprouts go with the ground. רבי יהודה: what sticks out is judged on its own. רבא's explanation fits both of their views in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And they follow their reasoning, as it is taught:
That which sprouts from the trunk and from the roots,
phrases.notes: The case is a tree owned by one person that grows on land owned by someone else.

phrases.english: these belong to the owner of the land.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
What sprouts from the trunk belongs to the owner of the tree,
and what sprouts from the roots belongs to the owner of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's framing in step 24 by showing the same split between the two תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי מאיר says the part sticking out follows the root and רבי יהודה does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about sprouts from the trunk and roots of a tree growing on another person's land
